procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Shaky hands since around October, both sides. Notices it holding his coffee and signing things; coworkers have commented. Says a beer in the evening calms it. No falls, no change in walking, no voice change. No new meds. Caffeine 2 cups/day.
BP still above goal. Fine bilateral tremor with arms outstretched, less at rest. Finger-nose ok. Normal tone, normal rapid alternating movements, gait normal.
A/P: bilateral action tremor, sounds like essential tremor (father had a tremor too) but would like neurology to confirm. TSH and BMP today. Referral placed. He's already on a beta-blocker for his heart.
HTN unchanged, discussed again, he wants to wait.

documents.title: Thyroid and kidney tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thyroid and kidney/electrolyte labs normal. Neurology should call you to schedule.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology practice. Date of service: 04/14/2021.
Reason for referral: hand tremor.

HPI: 58-year-old right-handed man with six months of tremor in both hands. It is most noticeable when he holds a cup of coffee or writes, and he has noticed it lessens after a drink. No head trauma and no seizures. No stiffness or slowness.

PMH: hypertension, coronary artery disease with LAD stent, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
Medications: lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide for blood pressure; also metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: his father had a tremor of the hands; no other movement disorder in the family.
Social: office administrator. Former smoker (quit 2013, 20 pack-years). One to two drinks a week.

Exam: BP 142/88. Alert, fluent. Cranial nerves intact. Postural tremor of both upper extremities, low amplitude, symmetric, with mild kinetic component on finger-nose. No rest tremor. Tone normal, no rigidity. No bradykinesia on finger taps. Strength, reflexes and sensation normal. Gait and tandem normal.

Data: recent routine labs and TSH from his primary care office normal.

Impression: essential tremor.
Plan: reassurance; he is already on a beta-blocker (metoprolol succinate) for cardiac reasons, and he does not want another medication now. Discussed adaptive strategies for writing and cups. Return as needed.

Outside neurology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over whether he'd qualify for the outside study of a new blood pressure medicine (saw the notice in our newsletter). BP has run above goal for the whole time I've known him on lisinopril 20 + HCTZ 25, home average about 145/91.
Neurology saw him for the tremor, essential tremor, no new medicine.
Went through the study criteria with him: uncontrolled pressure on 1-2 agents, stable cardiac disease - he fits on paper, final eligibility is the study team's call. Explained it is randomized and blinded, so he might get the study drug or a placebo on top of his usual pills, and that he keeps all his current medicines. Visits at the study site for 6 months. He'd like to do it.
Exam: BP above goal. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: HTN uncontrolled. Referral letter and recent labs sent to the study coordinator. Will see him for the baseline visit.

reports.text: 12-lead ECG. Rate 62. Normal sinus rhythm. PR 168 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 418 ms. Normal axis. No ST-T abnormality.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Trial Baseline Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Baseline visit for the blood pressure study; the study team asked for a resting ECG and a chemistry from us. He was accepted and randomized last week to study drug or placebo, blinded; the site dispenses it and he takes it in addition to his usual lisinopril and HCTZ. Primary endpoint is change in systolic pressure at 6 months.
Feels well. No palpitations in months.
BP above goal (recorded for the site). ECG: sinus rhythm, normal.
A/P: enrolled. No change in his own medicines. Baseline BMP today, results to the coordinator. He knows to call us or the site with any side effects.

documents.title: Study visits
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI the study wants me in every 4 weeks, last visit around Thanksgiving week. No problems with the pills so far. Do I need to tell the pharmacy?

documents.title: RE: Study visits
documents.author: RN
documents.body: No need to tell the pharmacy since the study supplies it. Just keep taking your regular medicines the same way. Thanks for the update.

orders.order: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
58 yo here for yearly exam. In the BP study, month 4 of 6. Feels ok, a bit more tired than usual the last few weeks, puts it down to work being busy. Tremor about the same.
No chest pain beyond usual, rare palpitations.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succ 50, ISMN 30, ASA 81, plus blinded study drug. NKDA.
Exam: BP above goal. Well appearing. Lungs clear, heart regular, abdomen soft and nontender, no edema. Fine postural tremor both hands.
A/P
- HTN: stays in the study through November, then reassess.
- Essential tremor: stable, no treatment wanted.
- CAD, pAF: stable.
- CRC screening: FIT never returned, closing that order. He agrees he really needs a colonoscopy; wants to finish the study first. Will bring it up again in the winter.
- Lung LDCT due next month, ordered. Flu shot today.
RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, office visit 11/02/2021.

Mr. Goodwin returns for his annual review. He is enrolled in an outside blood pressure study. Angina remains infrequent and unchanged with exertion; palpitations rare. BP 144/90, HR 64. Exam unremarkable. ECG: sinus rhythm, normal QRS and intervals.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg, aspirin 81 mg; blinded study medication. NKDA.

Impression: stable angina; paroxysmal AF, quiescent. Continue current therapy; one year.

Outside cardiology

documents.title: Study done + feeling run down
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the blood pressure study last Tuesday (11/23), they took me off the study pills. They won't tell me which one I had until the whole study is over. Separate thing - I've been really wiped out for a couple of months, sweating at night and I've lost weight without trying. Can I get in this week?

documents.title: RE: Study done + feeling run down
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know. The doctor wants to see you this week - you're booked Thursday 12/2 at 1:00. If you get a high fever, chest pain or feel faint before then, call us right away.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: Marked leukocytosis with left shift, anemia, thrombocytosis

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months of steadily worse fatigue. Wife told him he looks pale. Night sweats several nights a week, a few evenings of 99-100 F. Weight down about 6 kg since the physical without dieting. No cough, no urinary symptoms, no bleeding he's noticed, no chest pain. Off the study drug since 11/23.
Exam: pale. Weight 83 kg (89 in Sept). No lymphadenopathy in neck/axillae. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender, LUQ hard to assess with his body habitus. No rash or bruising.
A/P: constitutional symptoms with pallor. CBC with smear review and CMP now, stat.

Addendum 16:30: WBC 64.0 with a left shift - lab smear review shows metamyelocytes and promyelocytes. Hgb 8.5. Platelets 600. Called hematology on-call; urgent consult arranged for next week. Patient called (see phone note).

documents.title: Abnormal blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with CBC. Explained the white count is very high with immature cells, he is anemic and platelets high - this needs a blood specialist promptly; could be a bone marrow problem such as a leukemia, and they will sort out exactly what. Hematology/oncology appt Fri 12/10 at 10 am. ED precautions for fever over 101, bleeding, chest pain or fainting. He understood; wife on speaker.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with food and a full glass of water

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology consultation
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Outside hematology/oncology clinic. Date of service: 12/10/2021, with marrow results 12/14/2021.

Referred for leukocytosis with left shift, anemia and thrombocytosis.

HPI: 58-year-old man, three months of progressive fatigue, pallor, unintentional weight loss, night sweats and intermittent low-grade fevers.

PMH: hypertension, CAD with LAD stent 2016, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, essential tremor.
Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: father with hypertension, essential tremor and MI at 62; mother with type 2 diabetes.
Social: office administrator; former smoker, quit 2013; 1-2 drinks weekly.

Exam: HR 104. Pale conjunctivae. Spleen palpable below the left costal margin. No lymphadenopathy. Heart: mild tachycardia, regular. Lungs clear.

Labs: hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL; leukocytosis with left shift including metamyelocytes and promyelocytes; platelets 600,000/uL.

Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy (12/10/2021): hypercellular marrow with increased granulopoiesis; blasts not increased. BCR-ABL1 fusion detected by FISH and quantitative PCR.

Impression: chronic myeloid leukemia, BCR-ABL1 positive, chronic phase.

Plan: imatinib 400 mg daily started 12/14/2021 via our specialty pharmacy. CBC every 2 weeks initially, quantitative BCR-ABL1 every 3 months. Reviewed side effects (fluid retention, cramps, nausea, rash, cytopenias). Return in 4 weeks.

Outside hematology/oncology

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home. Hematology confirmed CML, chronic phase; on imatinib 400 daily since 12/14. A little queasy if he takes it without food, otherwise fine. Still tired, sweats a bit less. Lots of questions - went over what chronic phase means and that hematology will follow counts and the BCR-ABL level.
Med list updated with imatinib. Reminded him to run any new medicines or supplements past hematology because of interactions.
Vaccines: due for pneumococcal now that he's on cancer treatment - PCV20 at a nurse visit in January.
HTN, CAD, pAF unchanged. Study finished.
RTC 3 months, sooner prn.
